title: Biostatistics
description: Biostatistics develops the ability to learn from biological, clinical, and population-health data under uncertainty. Students move from well-posed questions and defensible designs to data exploration, probability, estimation, testing, regression, generalized models, survival analysis, reproducible computing, and responsible communication. The unified course uses one conceptual and computational core for all three degrees. Cases, data sets, and capstone choices provide Biology, Health Professions, and Public Health lenses.

resources.title: The Analysis of Biological Data
resources.description: Whitlock and Schluter. Biology-centered conceptual foundation, examples, experimental reasoning, and interpretation.

resources.title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
resources.description: Rosner. Comprehensive probability, inference, regression, survival, and clinical/health applications.

resources.title: Biostatistics: The Bare Essentials
resources.description: Norman and Streiner. Approachable explanations for Health Professions and Public Health learners.

resources.title: Intuitive Biostatistics
resources.description: Motulsky. Clear guidance on uncertainty, test interpretation, effect size, multiple comparisons, and common errors.

resources.title: Regression Methods in Biostatistics
resources.description: Vittinghoff et al. Bridge to linear, logistic, survival, repeated-measures, and applied health modeling.

resources.title: OpenIntro Statistics
resources.description: Free readings, exercises, data sets, labs, slides, and conceptual review.

resources.title: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
resources.description: Free foundation for description, probability, confidence intervals, tests, ANOVA, and regression.

resources.title: R for Data Science (2e)
resources.description: Free modern reference for importing, transforming, visualizing, and communicating data with R.

resources.title: R, RStudio, and Quarto

resources.title: UCLA OARC Statistical Consulting
resources.description: Applied guides for selecting and running methods in R, SAS, SPSS, and Stata.

resources.title: ASA GAISE College Report
resources.description: Course-design benchmark for statistical thinking, real data, technology, active learning, assessment, and ethics.

resources.title: Johns Hopkins Statistical Methods in Public Health I
resources.description: Official applied course objectives joining questions, probability, inference, displays, software, and interpretation.

resources.title: HHMI BioInteractive
resources.description: Authentic biology data, experiments, and classroom investigations.

resources.title: CDC Data and Epi Info
resources.description: Surveillance and population-health data plus an accessible epidemiologic analysis tool. Also https://www.cdc.gov/epiinfo/.

resources.title: BMJ Statistics Notes
resources.description: Short articles on interpreting common statistical methods in medical research.

resources.title: EQUATOR Network
resources.description: CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, and other design-specific reporting standards.

resources.title: NIH Rigor and Reproducibility
resources.description: Authoritative expectations for transparent, rigorous biological and health research.

resources.title: StatQuest
resources.description: Clear explanations of inference, regression, classification, validation, and statistical pitfalls.

resources.title: MarinStatsLectures
resources.description: Worked methods and R practice for applied statistics.

resources.title: Johns Hopkins Bloomberg SPH
resources.description: Public-health context and alternative explanations for biostatistical methods.

topics.title: Biostatistical Thinking, Data Types, and Research Questions
topics.description: This opening unit frames biostatistics as the discipline of learning from biological and health data under uncertainty. Students learn to connect research questions to variables, designs, and analyses.

children.title: Statistical reasoning in health and biology
children.description: Students learn why uncertainty is unavoidable in biological systems and health studies.

children.title: Types of variables
children.description: Students learn how variable type determines summaries, graphs, and statistical tests.

children.title: Research questions and hypotheses
children.description: Students learn to turn broad scientific curiosity into analyzable questions.

children.title: Data sources
children.description: Students learn how different data sources shape what can be inferred.

children.title: Estimands and operational definitions
children.description: Students learn to state precisely what quantity the study aims to estimate and how abstract concepts become measurable variables.

topics.title: Study Design, Sampling, Controls, Randomization, and Bias
topics.description: Study design determines the strength of conclusions before any calculation happens. Students learn how design choices protect against bias and support valid inference.

children.title: Observational and experimental designs
children.description: Students learn the major design families and what each can support.

children.title: Sampling and representativeness
children.description: Students learn how samples are selected and why representativeness matters.

children.title: Controls, replication, and randomization
children.description: Students learn how experiments separate treatment effects from noise.

children.title: Bias and validity
children.description: Students learn common threats to trustworthy results.

children.title: Measurement quality, ethics, and data-generating processes
children.description: Students learn that unreliable measurement, inappropriate collection, or unethical data practices cannot be repaired by sophisticated analysis.

children.title: Informed consent and secondary data use

topics.title: Descriptive Statistics and Data Visualization
topics.description: This unit teaches students to summarize and inspect data before formal modeling. Good description often reveals structure, errors, and questions worth testing.

children.title: Measures of center and spread
children.description: Students learn how to describe typical values and variability.

children.title: Distribution shape
children.description: Students learn to see skewness, outliers, and clustering.

children.title: Visualization for relationships
children.description: Students learn graphics for comparing groups and variables.

children.title: Data summaries by group
children.description: Students learn to compare patterns across treatment, exposure, or outcome groups.

topics.title: Probability, Probability Distributions, and Diagnostic Reasoning
topics.description: Probability gives the language for uncertainty. Students learn distributions and diagnostic concepts that appear throughout health and biological research.

children.title: Probability rules
children.description: Students learn how to reason about events and conditional information.

children.title: Common distributions
children.description: Students learn distributions used to model biological and health data.

children.title: Diagnostic testing
children.description: Students learn probability in the context of screening and diagnosis.

children.title: Bayes intuition
children.description: Students learn why pretest probability changes interpretation.

topics.title: Sampling Distributions, Estimation, Confidence Intervals, and Uncertainty
topics.description: This unit bridges samples to populations. Students learn how estimates vary and how confidence intervals express uncertainty.

children.title: Sampling distributions
children.description: Students learn why repeated samples produce different estimates.

children.title: Point estimation
children.description: Students learn how sample data estimate population parameters.

children.title: Confidence intervals
children.description: Students learn how intervals communicate plausible parameter values.

children.title: Interpreting uncertainty
children.description: Students learn what confidence intervals do and do not mean.

topics.title: Hypothesis Testing, P-Values, Effect Sizes, Power, and Sample Size
topics.description: This unit teaches the logic and limits of statistical testing. Students learn to pair significance with magnitude, design power, and practical interpretation.

children.title: Hypothesis testing framework
children.description: Students learn the standard steps of a statistical test.

children.title: Errors and power
children.description: Students learn the consequences of false positives and false negatives.

children.title: Effect size
children.description: Students learn to distinguish meaningful effects from merely detectable effects.

children.title: Sample size planning
children.description: Students learn how design assumptions affect needed sample size.

children.title: Multiplicity and selective reporting
children.description: Students examine how many outcomes, subgroups, or repeated tests can inflate false discoveries and distort a scientific story.

topics.title: Comparing Two Groups: Z-Tests, T-Tests, Paired Designs, and Nonparametric Alternatives
topics.description: This unit covers common comparisons between two groups or two time points. Students learn to choose tests based on outcome type, independence, and distribution assumptions.

children.title: One-sample and two-sample tests
children.description: Students learn basic mean comparisons.

children.title: Paired designs
children.description: Students learn why before-after or matched data need paired analysis.

children.title: Nonparametric alternatives
children.description: Students learn options when assumptions are weak or data are ordinal.

children.title: Health-science interpretation
children.description: Students learn how to report group comparisons responsibly.

topics.title: Comparing Multiple Groups: ANOVA, Multiple Comparisons, and Experimental Design
topics.description: This unit extends group comparisons to more complex designs. Students learn how ANOVA partitions variation and why multiple comparisons require care.

children.title: One-way ANOVA
children.description: Students learn how to compare means across three or more groups.

children.title: Post-hoc and multiple comparisons
children.description: Students learn why repeated testing inflates false positives.

children.title: Factorial designs
children.description: Students learn how experiments can test more than one factor.

children.title: Experimental design principles
children.description: Students connect ANOVA to design choices.

topics.title: Categorical Data Analysis: Proportions, Chi-Square Tests, Risk, and Odds
topics.description: Many biological and health outcomes are categories: diseased/not diseased, exposed/not exposed, improved/not improved. Students learn tools for counts, proportions, and association.

children.title: Proportions and contingency tables
children.description: Students learn how categorical data are organized.

children.title: Chi-square and exact tests
children.description: Students learn tests for association and goodness of fit.

children.title: Risk measures
children.description: Students learn effect measures used in epidemiology and clinical studies.

children.title: Screening and public health examples
children.description: Students practice interpreting categorical evidence.

topics.title: Correlation, Simple Linear Regression, and Model Interpretation
topics.description: This unit introduces relationships between continuous variables. Students learn how to describe association and fit a simple predictive or explanatory model.

children.title: Correlation
children.description: Students learn a standardized measure of linear association.

children.title: Simple linear regression
children.description: Students learn to model a continuous outcome with one predictor.

children.title: Model fit and assumptions
children.description: Students learn how to check whether a regression model is reasonable.

children.title: Interpretation
children.description: Students learn to explain regression in scientific language.

topics.title: Multiple Regression, Confounding, Interactions, and Model Diagnostics
topics.description: This unit teaches adjustment and multivariable thinking. Students learn how models account for additional predictors and how wrong models can mislead.

children.title: Multiple linear regression
children.description: Students learn to model outcomes with several predictors.

children.title: Confounding and adjustment
children.description: Students learn why crude associations can be misleading.

children.title: Interactions
children.description: Students learn when effects differ across groups or conditions.

children.title: Diagnostics and model selection
children.description: Students learn to evaluate and refine models.

children.title: Validation and prediction versus explanation
children.description: Students learn that a model that explains an association is not automatically a good predictor, and apparent fit can disappear in new data.

topics.title: Logistic, Poisson, Survival, and Other Generalized Models
topics.description: Health and biological outcomes often are binary, counts, or time-to-event rather than continuous. Students learn model families that match these outcome types.

children.title: Logistic regression
children.description: Students learn to model binary outcomes.

children.title: Poisson and count models
children.description: Students learn models for rates and counts.

children.title: Survival analysis
children.description: Students learn methods for time-to-event outcomes.

children.title: Generalized model framework
children.description: Students learn the common structure behind GLMs.

children.title: Clustered and longitudinal data overview
children.description: Students recognize when observations are correlated within people, clinics, communities, litters, sites, or repeated time points and why ordinary independence assumptions fail.

topics.title: Statistical Software, Reproducible Workflows, Missing Data, and Data Quality
topics.description: This unit makes biostatistics operational. Students learn how to conduct analyses transparently and detect data problems before they undermine results.

children.title: Statistical software workflow
children.description: Students learn basic analysis workflows in R, SAS, SPSS, or similar tools.

children.title: Reproducibility
children.description: Students learn practices that make analyses auditable and reusable.

children.title: Missing data
children.description: Students learn why missingness matters and how to describe it.

children.title: Data quality
children.description: Students learn to identify errors before modeling.

children.title: Sensitivity analysis, privacy, and responsible data stewardship
children.description: Students learn to test whether conclusions depend on cleaning or missing-data choices while protecting the people and communities represented in the data.

topics.title: Interpreting, Reporting, and Communicating Biostatistical Results
topics.description: The final unit turns analysis into scientific communication. Students learn how to present methods, results, uncertainty, and limitations to clinical, biological, or public-health audiences.

children.title: Statistical reporting
children.description: Students learn what belongs in a clear methods and results section.

children.title: Tables and figures
children.description: Students learn to communicate results visually and compactly.

children.title: Reporting standards
children.description: Students learn why guidelines improve transparency.

children.title: Audience-centered interpretation
children.description: Students learn to translate statistics into decisions and evidence statements.

children.title: Equity-aware interpretation and decision communication
children.description: Students learn to report subgroup evidence without hiding denominators, overstating unstable estimates, or framing inequity as an inherent trait of a population.
